question.text: The ionic radius of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Na</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math> ions is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>°</mo></mover><mo>.</mo></math> The ionic radii (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>°</mo></mover></math>) of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Mg</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Al</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> respectively, are

solution.text:
As we know nuclear charge increases, attraction of nucleus on electron increases because of that size decreases.

Here all ions have same number of electrons so as the number of protons increases nuclear charge increases and size decreases.

The ionic radii order is Na+>Mg2+>Al3+
